messages.subject: Interpreting interaction estimate from fitqtl
messages.body_plain:
Dear Dr. Karl Broman,

I have performed scantwo() on the RIL population and found significant evidence for interaction in cases case1 and case 2. When I fit the model for the pair of qtls for each case, I got a positive interaction estimate for each of them. How can I explain the direction of this interaction estimate with respect to the effect plot?

Thank You,
Pawandeep Singh

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Interpreting interaction estimate from fitqtl
messages.body_plain:
Code:
For Case1
qtl.1 <- makeqtl(cross_npmor.gp.sg <http://cross_npmor.gp.sg>, chr = c(2, 10),
                 pos = c(11.85097, 25.18568), what = "prob")
fit.1 <- fitqtl(cross_npmor.gp.sg <http://cross_npmor.gp.sg>, pheno.col = "TPPUE",
                qtl = qtl.1, method = "hk", get.ests = TRUE,
                formula = y ~ Q1*Q2)
summary(fit.1)

For Case2
qtl.2 <- makeqtl(cross_lpmor.gp.sg <http://cross_lpmor.gp.sg>, chr = c(6, 9),
                 pos = c(112.1284,127.7371), what = "prob")
fit.2 <- fitqtl(cross_lpmor.gp.sg <http://cross_lpmor.gp.sg>, pheno.col = "TPPUE",
                qtl = qtl.2, method = "hk", get.ests = TRUE,
                formula = y ~ Q1*Q2)

In case 2, additive effects of both the QTLs are negative, but the interaction effect is positive. How to explain this?

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Interpreting interaction estimate from fitqtl
messages.body_plain:
The additive effect is like the average phenotype for the BB genotype - average phenotype for AA genotype, averaged across genotypes at the 2nd locus.

The interactive effect is a difference [(ave when Q1=BB and Q2=BB) - (ave when Q1=AA and Q2=BB)] - [(ave when Q1=BB and Q2=AA) - (ave when Q1=AA and Q2=AA)].

Looking at your previous figures, we have, for both cases, (ave when Q1=BB and Q2=BB) > (ave when Q1=AA and Q2=BB)
while (ave when Q1=BB and Q2=AA) < (ave when Q1=AA and Q2=AA), and so the interaction effect in both cases should be positive.

For the additive effects of the individual loci, in case 1 things look pretty close to balanced and so I'd expect the additive effects to be small, and indeed the estimates are on the order of their standard errors, so confidence intervals would overlap 0.

In case 2, things look balanced for the S9 locus, while for S6 it looks like the AA genotype has higher phenotype than the BB genotype. So I'd expect S9 to have negligible additive effect, while S6 would have a negative additive effect, and that matches what you see.

karl

messages.subject: Re: Genetic map
messages.body_plain:
I would use summary() on the cross object, to ensure that it's being treated as a backcross ("bc") rather than an intercross ("f2").

R/qtl2 doesn't have a function for plotting maps, but the map objects are the same format as in R/qtl1, so you can use the R/qtl1 function, qtl::plotMap().

karl

messages.subject: Re: effectplot variance
messages.body_plain:
The effectplot() function returns a list with the means and standard errors.
Consider this example:

library(qtl)
data(fake.f2)
fake.f2 <- sim.geno(fake.f2, step=5, n.draws=8)
mname <- find.marker(fake.f2, 1, 37)
output <- effectplot(fake.f2, mname1=mname)
output$Means
output$SEs

karl

How can I be sure of ordering of the markers on each linkage group?

After estimating the recombination fraction using "est.rf" and "checkAlleles", i get the response "No apparent problems".

Also, please what can you say about the recombination fractions and lod score in the attached images?
